_doc: Declared adjustments to direction/sheet-briefs.json, applied at assembly time so the brief itself stays as it arrived and every change is readable beside its reason. Same pattern as direction/overrides.json for shot prompts. Every entry is class S - our staging - because none of it is established by the text.
_rule: An adjustment may change how something is SHOWN. It may never change what is claimed, who said it, or which evidence class a thing belongs to.

_framing.reason: Probe C proved the register question is real, and the first round of ten proved the answer was wrong. 'Photographic reference plate' bought photography and brought documentary with it: ten portraits of poor modern ascetics, shot like street photography. The text's Visvamitra is magnificent. A formal portrait under one warm light is a photograph too, and it is the right one.
_framing.with: A formal, dignified portrait photograph of a revered master, under one warm light: {shot}. Studio-lit, composed and still, in the manner of a portrait made to honour its subject. Not documentary, not street photography, not reportage, not concept art, not an illustration, not a painting. 9:16 vertical.
_framing.excludes: A character whose brief withholds the face is not a portrait subject - Kausalya's plate is her hands, and her own never-list forbids a portrait. She keeps the plate framing.

VISHVAMITRA._reason: The first round of ten failed at the brief, not the wording. Every candidate read as a poor modern ascetic - ragged, ash-caked, shot like reportage - because the brief asked for 'ash on the skin', 'matted', 'ochre', 'sun-weathered', and the framing asked for a documentary plate. The text does not describe a beggar. The description at Bala 20.10 (Dutt XXI) - dharma in bodily form, the foremost of the mighty, greatest in wisdom, the summit of austerity, mahateja, of great radiance - is spoken by VASISTHA to Dasaratha, not narrated, and the graph carries the locator with no claim on it. So the magnificence is a staging choice we take FROM a statement in the text, attributed to its speaker, and never presented as the narrator's description. He was born a king of the line of Kusika, and it should show.
VISHVAMITRA._direction_from: Laksh, 2026-09-22. The eye test is his: would a king rise from his throne to receive this man?
VISHVAMITRA._speaker_attribution: Bala 20.10 / Dutt XXI is VASISTHA speaking about Visvamitra. Nothing downstream may render it as narrator fact, and no copy may say 'the text describes him as' without naming Vasistha.

subject.value: a revered master in his sixties - a great sage who was born a king, of the line of Kusika. He carries himself like a man who ruled before he renounced
subject.reason: Replaces 'an ascetic sage'. The bearing is the whole correction: kingship before renunciation is textual and it is what the ten candidates had none of.

build.value: upright and broad-shouldered, physically strong. Lean from discipline, never gaunt and never starved. He holds his full height
build.reason: 'Lean and physically hard' drifted to emaciated on flux-pro, especially with ash. Naming the uprightness and the shoulders is what separates austerity from deprivation.

hair.value: long grey-white hair gathered and BOUND HIGH AS A CROWN at the top of the head - kept, ordered, dignified, tied close. A long full beard, grey-white, clean and well combed
hair.reason: 'Matted', and my own 'coiled rope-like locks', produced literal rope on nine of ten. Bound-as-a-crown is the same jata as a kept thing, which is what a master of austerity would have.

complexion.value: deep warm brown, even and healthy, and NONE LIGHTER. Skin that is looked after: no caking, no powder, nothing applied to it anywhere. His forehead is bare and clean
complexion.reason: The ash is gone entirely. It was the single worst instruction in the old brief: it lightened four of ten faces, caked two to grey-white, and pulled every candidate toward a street ascetic. The forehead is described as bare rather than by listing what must not be on it - naming a marking to forbid it put one on all ten.

dress.value: a black antelope skin over one shoulder; below it a simple bark-toned lower cloth, clean, deliberately draped and well kept. Clean, dignified, well-kept - never ragged, never torn, never impoverished. No saffron and no orange anywhere
dress.reason: Replaces the ochre cloth outright. Ochre read as modern saffron in every probe. The black antelope skin is the traditional ascetic's krsnajina: a named tradition, not something these sargas specify for him, and recorded as ours.

ornament.value: almost nothing. No jewellery, no beads across the chest, no pendant, no metal at the throat or wrist
ornament.reason: Three of ten hung mala and a brass pendant on him, because the brief named a rudraksa strand and the model rendered it as a display. Naming no chest ornament at all is more reliable than naming a discreet one.

the_one_thing.value: his eyes REST on what they look at, and there is authority in them. They do not search, they do not glare, and they do not plead.
the_one_thing.reason: Kept from the brief, with authority added. Several candidates resolved 'resting eyes' as either a stare or a weary gaze; neither is a man a king rises for.

value.how: hair bound high as a crown against hair combed and tied flat at the crown; a long full beard against a beard cut short; a black antelope skin over the shoulder against the sacred thread on a bare shoulder; bark-toned cloth against undyed white; broad and strong against older and softer

distinct_from.reason: Both men are now clean and dignified, so the contrast can no longer ride on dirty-against-clean or ochre-against-white. It moves to silhouette, beard length, the antelope skin and the thread - all of which survive at thumbnail size.

judging._doc: How a candidate is chosen, and in what order. Recorded because the order is a decision: a plate can be right in every listed particular and still be the wrong man.
order: THE EYE TEST FIRST, before any particular: would a king rise from his throne to receive this man? If the answer is no, nothing else about the plate matters.
THEN THE FACE. Is this a face that can carry fourteen shots and still be one person? Age in the neck and hands, eyes that rest with authority, no glare, no plea, no beatific smile.
Then the bearing: upright, broad-shouldered, full height. Lean from discipline, not starved.
Then the hair: gathered and bound high as a crown, kept and ordered. Not loose, not wild, and not rope.
Then the skin: deep warm brown, even, none lighter, nothing applied to it, forehead bare.
Then the dress: antelope skin over one shoulder, bark-toned lower cloth, clean and deliberately draped. Nothing ragged.

_world.reason: The universal world line reads 'Ornament from the relief vocabulary - heavy kundala earrings that pull the lobe, flat collars and torques, armlets above the bicep, bangles. Gold that gleams.' On a king that is right. On a renunciate it contradicts his own brief in the same prompt - 'No other ornament at all' and 'heavy kundala earrings' are both in there, and the model splits the difference. The line governs what ornament LOOKS LIKE when a character has any; it was never meant to require some. Made conditional, so it still binds Dasaratha and stops arguing with Visvamitra.
_world.replaces: Ornament from the relief vocabulary - Bharhut, Sanchi, Amaravati: heavy kundala earrings that pull the lobe, flat collars and torques, armlets above the bicep, bangles. Gold that gleams, never glitters. No faceted gems.
_world.with: Any ornament a character wears comes from the relief vocabulary - Bharhut, Sanchi, Amaravati: heavy kundala earrings that pull the lobe, flat collars and torques, armlets above the bicep, bangles. Gold that gleams, never glitters. No faceted gems. A character whose dress names no ornament wears none.

_views.reason: The framing now asks for one warm light and the front view slot still said 'even light'. Two lighting instructions in one prompt is the same defect as the ornament line that told an ascetic to wear kundala earrings - the model splits the difference. One warm key, evenly exposed, is what a formal portrait is.
_views.replaces: front view, full figure and head-and-shoulders, neutral standing, even light
_views.with: front view, full figure and head-and-shoulders, standing straight and still, evenly exposed
